title: Open Door
summary: A free-standing door stands ahead of the hovering aerial manipulator: an oak door panel in a metal frame, hinged on its left edge (as seen from the robot), with a metal lever handle near its right edge on the robot-facing side. Open the door: swing the panel on its hinge, away from the robot, by more than 20 degrees from closed.
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane; there is no wall, only the free-standing door assembly on the ground ahead of the robot. It consists of an immovable metal frame (two posts 2.0 m tall, 8 cm deep and 4 cm wide, about 1.4 m apart, joined at the top by a crossbar) and an oak panel 1.4 m wide, 2.0 m tall and 4 cm thick whose bottom edge is at ground level. The panel is hinged along the left post (as seen from the robot facing the door) about a vertical axis; it starts closed, in the plane of the frame, and can only swing away from the robot, up to 90 degrees open. It has no spring and no latch: it stays at whatever angle it is left, its motion resisted by hinge damping (which varies between instances) and a little joint friction. On the robot-facing side, near the free (right) edge and a little below mid-height, is a metal lever handle (a horizontal bar about 22 cm long standing about 11 cm proud of the panel) with a small round lock plate above it; the handle and the lock plate are visual only: they have no collision geometry. The door assembly's distance, sideways offset and yaw (turned by up to 15 degrees about the vertical) vary between instances. Nothing moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the door, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Door: articulation door.usd with a fixed root body DoorFrame (at the bottom centre of the frame), self-collisions disabled, solver iterations 4 position / 0 velocity; nominal root (1.0, 0.0, 0.0) m, orientation identity. At each reset (Isaac Lab mdp.reset_root_state_uniform) the root becomes (1.0 + dx, 0.0 + dy, 0.0) with dx, dy ~ U(-0.3, 0.3) m independently and orientation quat_from_euler_xyz(0, 0, yaw) with yaw ~ U(-pi/12, pi/12) rad (about the vertical through the root); AM-Bench's door_pos observation is this root position. In the door's frame (x away from the robot at yaw 0, y to the robot's left, z up): posts (convex-hull boxes) 0.08 (x) x 0.04 (y) x 2.0 (z) m centred at y = +0.7 and y = -0.7, z = 1.0; top bar (box) 0.08 x 1.44 x 0.04 m centred at z = 2.02. Panel (body DoorBody, convex-hull box) 0.04 x 1.4 x 2.0 m, closed it spans x -0.02..0.02, y -0.7..0.7, z 0..2.0; mass 1.0 kg (mass_props). Hinge: revolute joint 'Hinge' (DoorFrame to DoorBody) through (0, 0.7, z) in the door frame, axis the door frame's +z; limits [0, 90] degrees = [0, pi/2] rad; positive rotation (right-handed about +z) swings the free edge (y = -0.7) toward +x, away from the robot; reset to 0 rad (closed) with zero velocity every episode. Isaac Lab implicit actuator (replacing the USD drive): stiffness 0, damping 5.0 N m s/rad scaled at every reset by a factor ~ U(0.5, 2.0) (mdp.randomize_actuator_gains, so damping ~ U(2.5, 10)), joint friction 0.2 (static and dynamic), effort limit 20 N m. Handle (visual meshes without collision, attached to the panel; panel frame, closed): lever bar x -0.137..-0.127, y -0.52..-0.30, z 0.93..0.96, post and back plate (about y -0.58..-0.42, z 0.87..1.03) between it and the panel face; lock disc (visual only) about 6 cm across centred near (-0.023, -0.56, 1.15). No physics material is bound to the door: scene default friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0. Web assets: the panel's Oak.mdl and the frame's and handle's stainless-steel textures (Steel_Stainless base colour, normal and ORM PNGs) are loaded from NVIDIA's Omniverse content server.
success: Success when the revolute joint Hinge has position > 20 degrees = 0.349066 rad (door_opened_threshold_deg; strict inequality). The joint ranges from 0 rad (closed, its value at every reset) to pi/2 rad; positive is the panel's rotation about the vertical hinge axis that swings its free edge away from the robot. Nothing else is checked (the robot need not pass through the doorway). AM-Bench also reports subtask criteria door_engaged (joint position >= 0.05 x 0.349066 = 0.017453 rad) and door_opened (the success condition); they are informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 15 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 1800 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 1799th step.
difficulty_note: The 1.4 m panel has to be swung more than 20 degrees away from the robot by contact alone (the handle is decorative) from a free-flying, hovering base, and the door's position, yaw and hinge damping change per instance.
standard_notes: The door's pose (position and yaw), its hinge angle and hinge damping are not given: the frame and panel have to be located with the onboard cameras (the forward-looking airframe camera and the end-effector camera) and related to the robot through proprioception (base and end-effector poses). The opening angle can only be judged visually from the panel's position relative to the frame.
